stem: Before accepting an exception, a Klonopin prescription has been refilled six times within five months because the original stated six refills. What should the pharmacist recognize?

choices.text: Honor all six refills because they were written on the original after documenting whether practitioner notation could exceed the federal numerical limit.
Count only refills dispensed in Massachusetts.
Federal law limits Schedule IV prescriptions to five refills within six months, despite the prescriber's notation.
Allow another refill because five months is less than six months.
Convert the sixth refill into a partial fill of the fifth.

By contrast, 'Honor all six refills because they were written on the original.' would require that practitioner notation could exceed the federal numerical limit. The decisive cue appears in 'Before accepting an exception, a Klonopin prescription has been refilled six times within five months because the original stated six refills. What should the pharmacist recognize?'.

related_facts: clonazepam (Klonopin) is used for seizure disorders and panic disorder; it is federal Schedule IV and Massachusetts Schedule IV.
A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.
